headline: Anthropic asks D.C. appeals court to rehear Pentagon blacklisting case
body: Anthropic is asking a federal appeals court in Washington, D.C. to rehear its appeal of the Pentagon's blacklisting of its AI models, CNBC reports. The Defense Department labeled the company a supply chain risk in March, and the D.C. Circuit upheld the blacklisting in a 2-1 decision in September. A Pentagon spokesperson told CNBC that the agency doesn't comment on pending or ongoing litigation.
note: The label blocks defense contractors from using Anthropic's technology in their work with the agency. For finance teams that work with defense contractors, a government designation of an AI vendor can reach their own supply chain.

evidence.text: Anthropic is asking a federal appeals court in Washington, D.C. to rehear its appeal in a case concerning the Pentagon's blacklisting of the company's AI models.
The Defense Department labeled Anthropic a supply chain risk in March, and the AI company sued the Trump administration in an effort to undo that action.
In September, the D.C. Circuit upheld the Pentagon's blacklisting.
The 2-1 decision rejected Anthropic's argument that the Department of Defense's ban on its Claude models was arbitrary, unauthorized and unconstitutional.
A Pentagon spokesperson told CNBC in an email that the agency doesn't comment on pending or ongoing litigation.
The Defense Department, led by Pete Hegseth, applied the supply chain risk label in March, a move that blocked defense contractors from using the company's technology in their work with the agency.
